# Draft:Letter of the King of Sweden in 1711

The 1711 letter recognizing Ukraine as an independent state stands as a pivotal document in Ukrainian-Swedish diplomatic history.
Written by King Charles XII of Sweden following the  in July 1711, the letter formally acknowledges Ukraine’s independence and Pylyp Orlyk as Hetman of Ukraine. Charles XII also affirmed the Constitution of Ukraine of 5 April 1710 and declared himself its protector. In this letter, dated 14 September 1711, the king instructed Thomas Funck, Sweden's extraordinary envoy to Constantinople, to advocate for Ukraine’s sovereignity during negotiations with the Sultan. Funck and the Sultan were to demand that Peter I honor his 1711 post-capitulation pledge to recognize Ukraine's independence. The letter serves as a powerful testament to the enduring Ukrainian-Swedish alliance, a tradition first established by Charles X and Bohdan Khmelnytsky.
Documents from the Military Chancellery in Bender: National Archives of Sweden
In July 1716, four chests of documents from the newly established Ministry of Foreign Affairs—a branch of Charles XII's Military Chancellery—were transported from Bender (then Ottoman Empire) to Ystad, a town in southern Sweden. These documents were later moved from Ystad to Stockholm, where they became part of the archives of the old royal chancellery.
The chests contained critical correspondence spanning from August 1709, following the Swedish retreat from Poltava to Bender, to October 1714, when the Swedish army departed the Ottoman Empire, with additional documents from 1715. Among the preserved records are:
* 10. Five packages of letters from Thomas Funck (1711– 1713)
* 11. One package of draft decisions for Funck (1711–1713)
* 25. A package of Cossack letters (1713–1714)
* 26. A package of draft decisions and letters addressed to Cossack leaders (1709–1715)
* 46. Original letters from the Sultan
* 49. Letters from the Grand Viziers (Süleyman Pasha and Ibrahim Pasha) and the Tatar Khan
* 54. Two packages of intercepted letters
Discovery and Popularization in Ukraine
In early September 2021, Ukrainian history researcher Marina Trattner asked Jan Mispelaere, a historian and archivist at the Swedish State Archives to locate documents confirming Charles XII’s support for Ukraine in its struggle for independence. After a thorough search, Mispelaere identified the document in question. Trattner publicly announced the discovery on 8 September 2021. A copy of the letter was forwarded to Andrii Plakhotniuk, Ukraine's Ambassador to Sweden.
After the exhibition Rarities of the Ukrainian Cossack State—Hetmanate of the 17th–18th Centuries: To the 30th Anniversary of Ukraine's Independence, photographs of the 1711 letter were gifted to St. Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv as a gesture from Sweden.
On 4 July 2022, during her visit to Kyiv, Swedish Prime Minister Eva Magdalena Andersson personally presented a facsimile of this letter to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The event garnered widespread media attention, though some reporters conflated the Ukrainian Cossack state (Zaporizhian Host) as referenced in the letter, with the Zaporozhian Sich (the autonomous enclave of the Zaporizhian Army within it).

Quotes
Original (In Swedish):
5: Sammaledes har han at pådrifwa, det den Artikeln som talar om Ukrains och Samptelige Zaporovernes frijhet må bringas ofördröijeligen til sin fullkomlige wärkställighet, så at hela Ukraine ock den Zaporowiske-hären fullkombligen sättas uti des urgamla frijhet ock possession af des land ock förra gränsor under des nu warande fältherre Philipp Orlick: på det sättet at bemälte folck hädan effter skall giöra en independent Stat, ock aldrig mer på något sätt stå under Czarens lijdno eller protection.
In Ukrainian:
5: Водночас він має наполягати на тому, щоб ця Стаття, яка затверджує свободу України і всіх Запорожців, негайно ж і повністю стала чинною, щоб таким чином вся Україна і Військо Запорозьке в повному обсязі отримали давні свободи і вольності, а також отримали власність землею у своїх давніх кордонах під керівництвом теперішнього гетьмана Пилипа Орлика; так, щоб народ, який описаний вище, одразу ж отримав статус незалежної Держави, і більше ніколи і жодним чином не був під послухом Царя чи його протекцією.
